title: Woman who helped Abby Choi's ex-husband to flee Hong Kong after murder loses appeal, jailed 6 months

 Woman who helped Abby Choi's ex-husband to flee Hong Kong after murder loses appeal, jailed 6 months
 She had arranged for him to leave Hong Kong by speedboat from Tung Chung Pier.
 Khine Zin Htet 
 November 16, 2026, 07:10 PM
Photo from HK01 and xxabbyc/Instagram
 The woman who helped Hong Kong socialite Abby Choi’s ex-husband, Alex Kwong, flee the city has lost her appeal against her conviction. 
 Influencer Irene Poon, also known as Poon Hiu-yin, must serve six months in jail for conspiracy to pervert the course of justice. 
 Choi was allegedly murdered by Kwong, his father and his brother in February 2023. 
 The murder trial involving the three men is ongoing. 
 According to TVB , case documents stated that between Feb. 24 and 25, 2023, Poon and another woman helped Kwong leave Hong Kong by speedboat from Tung Chung Development Pier. 
 Poon was convicted in June 2026 and sentenced to six months’ imprisonment. 
 She subsequently appealed against both her conviction and sentence. 
 On Nov. 16, a High Court judge ruled that Poon had played a “pivotal role” in the case by actively relaying messages and providing advice. 
 The judge dismissed her appeal and ordered her to serve her sentence immediately. 
 Helped Choi’s ex-husband flee Hong Kong
 According to HK01 , Poon conspired with a woman named “Ivy” to help Kwong leave Hong Kong through unofficial and unlawful means. 
 In her appeal, Poon's lawyer claimed that Ivy had misled her by presenting Kwong as a legitimate businessman rather than a wanted criminal. 
 The lawyer also said Poon had assumed Kwong was the boyfriend of another influencer. 
 Poon's lawyer further argued that her role was less significant than that of her co-defendant, Lam Shun, and that her sentence should therefore be reduced. 
 Lam, an employee of a yacht company, was also convicted and sentenced to six months’ imprisonment. 
 Judgment
 The judge found that Poon had relayed a message stating that riding without going through customs would cost HKD$30,000 (S$4,927) and that the money had to be transferred first if they needed to leave immediately. 
 She had also received messages such as “need to arrange to charter two boats” and “any amount of money is no problem”. 
 During the trial, Poon continued to deny knowing about the route and arrangements for an irregular departure, despite evidence in her messages suggesting otherwise. 
 Addressing Poon’s claim that she did not know Kwong’s identity, the judge said the evidence, including messages referring to “illegal border crossing” and “bypassing customs”, showed that Poon knew Kwong needed to leave Hong Kong to evade law enforcement. 
 Despite this, she continued to actively assist him. 
 The judge also found that Poon had played a pivotal role, as Ivy and Kwong would not have been able to contact Lam without her involvement.
